nodes.description: Public array of IPFS phase hashes used to build token URIs.
Public mapping storing the mint timestamp of each token id.
Public mapping flagging tokens that rolled the 'rare' branch.
Private Counters.Counter used to allocate sequential token ids.
Constant payable address that receives all ETH sent to claim().
Public mint price in wei, increased by 3% on every claim.
Payable mint entry point: forwards msg.value, raises price, mints token and records birth/rare.
View function returning the phase based URI computed from token age.
Constructor initializing ERC721 name/symbol, base URI and price.
Caller-controlled origin of claim(), used as mint recipient.
Miner-influenced timestamp used for birth records, rarity roll and age calculation.
Low-level value call buidlguidl.call{value: msg.value}("") executed inside claim().
Unchecked arithmetic expression price = (price * 103) / 100.
Time dependency: age = block.timestamp - birth[tokenId] and blockhash based randomness.
tokenId argument of tokenURI(uint256).
Local variable id holding the freshly allocated token id in claim().
Local bool capturing the success flag of the buidlguidl value call.
Local age of a token in seconds inside tokenURI().
Local string holding the selected phase hash in tokenURI().
Local string holding baseURI() in tokenURI().

edges.reason: claim() transfers msg.value to an external address through a low-level call before all state updates are finalized.
The value call hands control to buidlguidl, which could re-enter claim() before price/token state is settled.
price is read and multiplied by 103 inside the unchecked fee escalation expression.
The recomputed price is written back to storage without SafeMath, allowing silent overflow.
msg.sender is used as the recipient of the newly minted token.
block.timestamp is stored into birth[id] and feeds the blockhash-based rarity roll, making outcome miner-influenceable.
block.timestamp and blockhash(block.number-1) drive the pseudo-random rarity decision and the age calculation.
tokenURI branches on age derived from block.timestamp, i.e. on miner-controlled time.
buidlguidl is the destination address supplied to the low-level value call.
claim() increments the _tokenIds counter to allocate a new id.
claim() may write true into the rare mapping for the new token id.
claim() writes the current block.timestamp into the birth mapping for the new token id.
tokenURI reads block.timestamp to compute how old the token is.
tokenURI reads birth[tokenId] to derive the token age.
tokenURI reads rare[tokenId] to choose the final phase hash.
tokenURI selects one of the entries in the phases array.
The constructor/initializer sets the initial mint price.
The tokenId parameter is consumed by tokenURI for existence and lookup queries.
claim() assigns the counter value to the local token id variable.
The local id is used as the key when recording the birth timestamp.
The local id is used as the key when setting the rare flag.
tokenURI computes the token age into a local variable.
The low-level call return value is captured in the sent local variable.
tokenURI assigns the chosen phase hash to the local _tokenURI string.
tokenURI reads baseURI() into the local base string.

normalization_plan.reason: The tokenId parameter has no independent security meaning and is fully absorbed into the tokenURI function node.
The local id is a transient handle created and consumed inside claim(), so it collapses into the claim function node.
The sent flag is only the success indicator of the buidlguidl value call and merges into that unsafe_operation.
The age local is an intermediate computation used only inside tokenURI and folds into the tokenURI node.
The _tokenURI local is the return buffer of tokenURI and merges into the tokenURI function node.
The base local is a temporary copy of baseURI() used only in tokenURI and merges into the tokenURI node.
